source: EthioJobs, HaHuJobs, Ethiopian Reporter Jobs, PalmJobs, DevNetJobs, HarmeeJobs, ElelanaJobs, KebenaJobs, Afriworket, GeezJobs, NGOJobs, X (Grok search), ReliefWeb

taxonomies.jobs: ISCO-08 (ILO International Standard Classification of Occupations)
taxonomies.education: ISCED 2011 (UNESCO International Standard Classification of Education)
taxonomies.sectors: ISIC Rev.4 (UN International Standard Industrial Classification)

notes.education_specializations: Field-of-study is extracted from free-text descriptions, which only HaHuJobs postings have — EthioJobs postings contribute to each level's total but rarely to a specific field.
notes.employer_type: Private / Public / NGO is a keyword heuristic on the employer's own name, not a verified registry lookup.
notes.critical_skills: A sub-sector or role only appears here once at least 3 of its postings state a skills_required value, so a top-3 list is never built from a single posting.
notes.employer_registry: Employer names are grouped by stripping legal suffixes and punctuation before counting, so minor spelling differences for the same employer are merged. This is a text heuristic, not a verified business registry lookup.
notes.region: Region is inferred from a keyword lookup against the location field a posting already states. A location this lookup does not recognize, including a bare country name or Remote, is left unclassified rather than guessed.
notes.language: Language is classified from the Unicode script of each posting's title and description text. This tells English from Ethiopic script reliably, but does not distinguish Amharic from Tigrinya or any other language written in that script.
notes.dates: Posting and deadline dates written as 5 hours ago or 12 Days Left are converted using the scrape time of the same row, with a month taken as 30 days. Status is open when the deadline date has not passed on the day the rollup runs and unknown when no deadline is stated.
notes.employer_classes: Names such as Company and Private Client hide the employer, and Talent Search is a recruiting intermediary. Both are left out of employer rankings and counted on their own line.
notes.classification_coverage: Each figure is the share of a source's postings for which the field could be filled or classified. A low figure points to what the source supplies or what the classifiers recognise.
notes.positions: Postings are advertisements. Positions are the vacancies a posting says it fills. Only postings that state a number of positions between 1 and 100 are summed. Larger numbers are reported on their own line, and a posting that states none counts as one position in the lower bound.
notes.experience_barrier: Uses the lower end of the stated range, so 1 to 3 years counts as 1 year. Postings that state no number are shown as not stated and are not read as requiring no experience.
notes.skill_types: A posting counts once per type if it states at least one skill of that type. Types come from keyword rules on the normalised skill text, and skills the rules do not recognise fall under technical or occupation specific.
notes.location: Location is standardised to Town, Region. The town is the first town named in the posting and the region is its regional state. NC, Region means No City, because the posting named only a region or zone. Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa are chartered cities that are also regional level administrations, so their label repeats the name. Unspecified means the posting names no place in Ethiopia. Postings that list several towns are counted once, under the first town. A town missing from the gazetteer is labelled Region not identified and listed so it can be added. Regions follow the states in force since 2023.
notes.subcategories: Subcategories are one fixed list of 24 groups plus Other and not classified, and postings with no tag are shown as Not stated. Each site tag maps to exactly one group, so Finance, Accounting and Accounting and Finance fall in one group, as do Business and Business Administration. A posting is counted once, under its first tag that the list recognises. Bars therefore add up to the postings counted and no posting is counted twice.
notes.salary_transparency: Figure means the posting states an amount. Wording means it says only that pay is negotiable or follows a scale. Shares are of all postings in the period. Tracking began in September 2026 and one week holds a large first load, so changes over time partly reflect which sources were added when, not only employer behaviour.
notes.concentration: Top 5 and top 10 share and the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI) describe how concentrated postings are among the leading skills, employers or categories this window, not whether that concentration reflects a genuine shortage.
